etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English fansy, fantsy, a contraction of fantasy, fantasye, fantasie, from Old French fantasie, from Medieval Latin fantasia, from Late Latin phantasia (“an idea, notion, fancy, phantasm”), from Ancient Greek φαντασία (phantasía), from φαντάζω (phantázō, “to render visible”), from φαντός (phantós, “visible”), from φαίνω (phaínō, “to make visible”); from the same root as φάος (pháos, “light”); ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰh₂nyéti, from the root *bʰeh₂- (“to shine”). Doublet of fantasia, fantasy, phantasia, and phantasy.

definitions.definition: The imagination.

definitions.definition: An image or representation of anything formed in the mind.

definitions.definition: In the game of jacks, a style of play involving additional actions (contrasted with plainsies).

quote.citation: 1970, Marta Weigle, Follow my fancy: the book of jacks and jack games, page 22:
quote.text: When you have mastered plainsies, the regular jack game, and have learned all the rules, you will be ready to use this part of the book. A fancy is a variation of plainsies which usually requires more skill than plainsies does.

quote.citation: 2002, Elizabeth Dana Jaffe, Sherry L. Field, Linda D. Labbo, Jacks, page 26:
quote.text: When you get good at jacks, try adding a fancy. A fancy is an extra round at the end of a game. It makes the game a little harder. Jack Be Nimble, Around the World, or Black Widow are some fancies.

Of a superior grade.
Executed with skill.
(colloquial) Unnecessarily complicated.
(obsolete) Extravagant; above real value.

quote.text: This anxiety never degenerated into a monomania, like that which led his [Frederick the Great's] father to pay fancy prices for giants.

definitions.definition: (nonstandard) In a fancy manner; fancily.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English fancien, fantasien, fantesien, from Old French fantasier, from the noun (see above)).

definitions.definition: (formal) To appreciate without jealousy or greed.
(British) Would like; have a desire for.
(British, informal) To be sexually attracted to.
